newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar trims gains as NY rally falters.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar trims gains as NY rally falters.

text.p: White sugar futures pared some of their earlier gains in light Wednesday activity and traders continued to look for fresh sign of physical offtake to snap the London market out of its lethargy. Most attention was centred on the white premium and the raws market after its recent rally but New York's failure to sustain upside momentum was said to have dampened sentiment on the whites market and encouraged light profit-taking.

"The general feeling within the trade is that the white premiums are still overvalued and therefore will narrow," one trader said, adding that London was likely to either hold steady or slip depending on the fortunes of the raws.
At 1626 GMT values of the March and May contracts stood very close to each other and hovered near intraday highs.
March was $2.40 higher at $304.00 and May moved higher to be marginally more expensive, up $2.30 at $304.10.
Other traded positions were also firmer and overall volume totalled a light 666 lots, mainly composed of crossed trades from the morning.
Elsewhere, the EU awarded 45,400 tonnes of current series white sugar with export rebates of a maximum 47.002 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at its weekly tender.

Poland's Agriculture Ministry said it wanted to raise the quota for domestic sugar sales by 130,000 tonnes to 1.63 million tonnes for the 1996/1997 growing season to help absorb this year's sugar surplus.
The Paris market saw subdued activity with a light turnover of 288 lots. March was down 40 cents at $303.60 and May down $1.00 at $303.50.
